Sasha (Finance Ops): Hey team — vendor 'BlueAnchor' sent invoice 2023-089. Invoice in EUR but they want to be paid in USDT. Invoice shows VAT ID NL123456789B01 and a note 'supply of software - B2B'. They also have a line 'nonresident supplier / BlueAnchor US Inc'. Can tax confirm whether we treat this as reverse-charge or if VAT is due? Also vendor asked about gross-up for any withholding.

Ivan (Tax Lead): Crypto as payment medium doesn't change VAT rules. If it's B2B and the place of supply is the customer's location (us in EU), reverse charge normally applies provided the vendor has a valid EU VAT ID. If the legal entity is actually a US corp, they shouldn't be invoicing under an NL VAT ID unless there's a Dutch branch. Need verification (VIES screenshot + registration docs). For withholding: normally software licenses supplied cross-border from non-EU to EU don't trigger EU VAT withholding, withholding rules depend on payee tax residence and local rules — if they're a US tax resident we'd normally ask for W-9.

Sasha (Finance Ops): attaching invoice snippet for context:
```
Invoice: 2023-089-USDT
Vendor: BlueAnchor Ltd / BlueAnchor US Inc
VAT: NL123456789B01
Amount: EUR 12,500
Payment terms: 14 days (payment via USDT)
Notes: "nonresident supplier; no VAT charged"
```

Olivia (Vendor Ops): Quick Q from AP — can we process an invoice that lists both a US entity and an EU VAT ID? They say they have a Dutch branch. Also, do we need a W-9/W-8 for crypto payouts? Payment will route via Coinbase Prime.

Ivan (Tax Lead): If there's a Dutch branch then the VAT ID may be legitimate — but we need evidence: 1) VIES verification screenshot, 2) which legal entity the invoice is for (company registration number and legal name), and 3) statement showing the VAT treatment (they should indicate 'reverse charge' or 0% B2B). Crypto payout does not obviate tax-doc requirements. If the invoiced legal entity is US-based, request W-9. If Dutch branch is the supplier, ask for incorporation excerpt.

Taxbot: VIES check NL123456789B01 => valid (VIES snapshot: 2023-11-08) :white_check_mark:

Matt (Accounting): A few practical items — how do we record crypto-denominated payment for VAT reporting? We typically record VAT on the EUR invoice amount and convert any crypto settlement to EUR using the exchange rate on the date of supply. Also: should AP block payment until docs are received?

Ivan (Tax Lead): Correct — use the EUR invoice amount for VAT records, capture FX on date of supply. Hold payment until docs are confirmed. On gross-up: our standard policy is not to automatically gross-up withholding unless there's an explicit contract clause approved by Legal/RevOps. If vendor asks for gross-up, escalate to Legal and the vendor's account owner.

Sasha (Finance Ops): I just messaged vendor — asked them to reissue with the definitive legal entity (company reg #), attach proof of VAT (VIES screenshot or certificate), and provide tax residence docs (W-9 for US entity or NL branch certificate). Notifying AP to put payment on hold until we receive. /cc @Ivan @Matt

Olivia (Vendor Ops): Will request now, vendor ETA ~48h :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Ivan (Tax Lead): I'll draft our standard request template for cross-border crypto vendors and paste it here once done. Also will note escalation path for gross-up requests.

Sasha (Finance Ops): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
